title: What is CSAIL?
slide_intent: Give a mission statement human scope by naming who the organization serves. Readers can then connect an institutional purpose to recognizable communities.
strategic_value: CSAIL can relate computing research to its intended effect on people while giving writers a set of values against which to judge tone.
demonstration: Mission and audiences occupy the middle column, values occupy the right, and a large orange statement repeats the mission low on the page.
practical_value: Use the named audiences and values to decide which part of a lab story matters to a particular reader.

content_islands.name: Page question
content_islands.spec: Set the question in the narrow left column, leaving space below for the larger mission statement.

content_islands.name: Mission and audiences
content_islands.spec: Use a short mission paragraph and a list covering MIT, the nation and the human community.

content_islands.name: Values
content_islands.spec: Arrange the five values as a separate vertical list at right, with an explanation under each name.

content_islands.name: Mission statement
content_islands.spec: Repeat the central claim in large, light orange type below the left columns.
